verdict.line: You lose if you feed K'Sante free Q stacks and eat his W stun into an all-in before level 6; you win if you survive to the health-stacking items and turn skirmishes into sustain fights.

brief.thesis: K'Sante holds lane priority and the solo-kill edge because his Q (Ntofo Strikes) builds stacks into a pull and his W (Path Maker) stun chains directly into damage, while Mundo's own tools are trade-and-sustain tools that only pay off once he's already stacked health. The measured 47.7% win rate over 199 games reflects a lane that's lost early and clawed back mid-game: Adrenaline Rush's passive regen and E (Masochism)'s missing-health AD scaling mean Mundo starts winning extended skirmishes once tank items come online, which is also why the overall matchup shape is rated even despite the lane deficit.

theirWindow.what: He takes reduced damage while charging up, then dashes to knock back and stun. Step out of the dash arc or call for help before the charge finishes — the window right after is when his all-in actually lands.

yourWindow.what: E (Masochism) scales bonus AD off your missing health, and Adrenaline Rush is already regenerating a percentage of your max health every second, so this is when you commit to trades — your sustain outlasts his burst in extended exchanges, not single pokes.

start.why: Absorbs K'Sante's Q (Ntofo Strikes) poke at 450 range and keeps you from getting zoned out before level 3.

boots.why: The extra move speed lets you step out of W (Path Maker)'s dash arc and close distance for Q (Infected Cleaver) poke without trading into his stun range.

core.why: Raw health pool compounds with Adrenaline Rush's percentage regen, which is the single biggest lever you have in this matchup.
Converts the health you're already stacking into stat gains and gives you a reason to keep building tanky instead of forcing damage items.
Amplifies both Adrenaline Rush and E (Masochism)'s sustain-heavy trade pattern once skirmishes start running long.

situational.when: you're ahead on health stacking and need more dueling damage to close out skirmishes
K'Sante or another enemy carry is building around sustained auto-attacks
their team has a crit or attack-speed carry punishing your sustain fights

runes.keystoneWhy: Rewards the exact trade pattern this matchup wants — standing in melee range while K'Sante pokes you with Q, since Grasp heals you back and grows your max health off the same trades he's trying to win.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport is the higher-win-rate pairing here (47.6% over the two most-run options): Flash gives you an out from W (Path Maker)'s stun/knockback, and Teleport lets you reset for health-stacking items and still make the lane relevant after falling behind early.

playing.title: Deny the second Q stack
playing.detail: Don't stand still for a second hit of Ntofo Strikes — at 2 stacks it fires a shockwave that pulls you in, which is how he opens most of his all-ins.

playing.title: Back off during his W charge
playing.detail: Path Maker's charge-up reduces the damage he takes, then dashes into a knockback and stun. Step out of the dash line before it fires instead of trying to trade through it.

playing.title: Commit low, not full health
playing.detail: E (Masochism) scales AD off missing health and your passive is already regenerating percent max health every second, so your best trades happen when you're already hurt, not when you're topped off.

playing.title: Toggle W before he stuns you
playing.detail: Burning Agony reduces the duration of disables, so turning it on before his W connects shortens the stun window he's trying to lock you down with.

playing.title: Poke at 975, not 525
playing.detail: Q (Infected Cleaver) outranges his E (Footwork) dash-and-shield by a wide margin — force him to walk up into your cleaver range instead of letting him dictate when trades start.

playing.title: Save Sadism for skirmishes
playing.detail: R's move speed and regen burst are wasted in a straight duel — hold it for extended 2v2s or objective fights where the sustain actually outlasts his cooldowns.

playing.title: Rush the health-stacking core
playing.detail: Warmog's into Heartsteel is what flips this matchup from a losing lane into an even one — prioritize it over damage items even if you're slightly behind.

brief.patchCaveat: The build, runes, summoners, and win rates above are measured from real games on the current patch (16.20.1) via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning — why each cooldown, stack, and trade window matters — is my own tactical read, not scraped data.
